notes: The bioRxiv connector returns 30 results per page whatever limit is set, so the README rule 'page until fewer than 100' would stop after page 1. I paged with cursor steps of 30 until a page came back empty or short (bioinformatics 7 pages, genomics 3, cancer biology 3, genetics 1).
PubMed returns very long metadata for ~270 papers; I screened titles first and read abstracts only for the shortlist.

None of the three featured papers has an open licence (PubMed shows no CC BY), so all three got hand-drawn illustrations instead of Figure 1. The PubMed MCP does not expose figure files, so I did not try to download any.

Unclear in rules: Tier 1 'post every purely computational paper' conflicts with the out-of-scope line on protein design; I followed the out-of-scope line. Also unclear whether papers that mention chordoma only as a differential diagnosis count as Chordoma; earlier runs said yes, so I applied that.
Preprint 10.64898/2026.06.30.735642 is a v2 of a July preprint whose DOI was never posted, so it counts as new under the README rule.
Preprint chordoma screening is by title and the 100-character abstract preview only, so a chordoma mention deeper in an abstract could be missed.

notes: bioRxiv search_preprints returns at most 30 matches per call and its cursor counts matches within the chosen category, so the README's limit=100 with cursor 0, 100, 200 skips matches 30-99, 130-199 and so on. This run used limit=30 with cursor 0, 30, 60 until an empty page: bioinformatics 237 preprints, genomics 49, cancer biology 86, genetics 23. README step 3 should be updated.
PubMed get_article_metadata returns at most 20 articles per call, so about 270 PMIDs took 14 calls.

The Cell centromere k-mers paper is a method plus a cancer-translocation finding; it was given the main topic Cancer genomics, but the topic rules do not say how to place a method paper with a disease finding.
The m6A nanopore preprint (10.1101/2025.11.02.686099) is listed as v6 with a new title, but get_preprint returned the v1 abstract, so the summary uses that abstract with the current title.
Circle-Seq (RNA) and ANCOM-BC (Bioinformatics) were left out as microbial work; the rules do not say whether a general-purpose statistics tool for microbiome data counts as Methods.

notes: The bioRxiv connector returned HTTP 500 errors on many calls (search_preprints and get_preprint); I retried until each shortlisted DOI and each category/day range returned. Pages came back 30 at a time rather than 100 and paging by cursor 30/60 worked, so the README step 3 rule 'stop when a page has fewer than 100 results' does not apply to this connector.
Preprints dated 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08 were sparse in the listings, so the last two days may be under-covered.
No Figure 1 downloads: PubMed lists the three featured Nature papers as 'The Author(s)' with no open licence, so all three pictures are hand-drawn illustrations.

Chordoma rule: the one chordoma post is a clival chondrosarcoma case report that only mentions chordoma as the initial suspected diagnosis; it counts under the 'mentions chordoma in the abstract' rule.
Several preprints in the listings are revisions (v2, v3) of older DOIs; none of the DOIs had been posted before, so they were treated as new.
